steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on Diff-KPE, a keyphrase extraction model that uses a text diffusion process and a supervised information bottleneck to improve phrase representations. Cover existing KPE approaches, the gap we see, how Diff-KPE works and its advantages, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Keyphrase extraction (KPE): definition and uses
- Existing approaches: sequence labeling, phrase classification, ranking
- Gap: phrase representations don't use reference keyphrase information
- Diff-KPE: diffusion model, ranking network, supervised VIB
- Advantages and contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- KPE
  - extract several present keyphrases that highly summarize document
  - helpful for text summarization, information retrieval
- Existing approaches
  - token-level sequence labeling, single label per token (cite)
  - phrase classification, labels for text spans, phrase-level semantics (cite)
  - recent: directly learn to rank phrases (cite)
  - two processes: candidate phrase representation construction + keyphrase importance ranking
  - representations from token embeddings of pre-trained LMs, e.g. BERT (cite)
  - ranking: score per candidate, margin loss, positives ahead of negatives
  - ways to extract phrase representation: Bi-LSTM (cite) and CNN (cite) for local-aware features; HyperMatch (cite): hyperbolic space
- Gap
  - great success on benchmarks, but representations lack reference keyphrase information
  - intuition from humans: review whole document, summarize vague keyphrases in mind, then consider candidate + vague keyphrases
  - challenge: generate vague reference keyphrase info at inference time
- Diff-KPE
  - novel diffusion-based KPE model
  - diffusion model recovers reference keyphrase embeddings conditioned on document -> vague keyphrase info
  - inject vague keyphrase embeddings into each phrase representation
  - ranking network ranks enhanced representations; extract top k
  - supervised Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB): classification loss per phrase; keep target-class info, filter irrelevant input info (cite); helps learn vague keyphrase embedding
  - multitask learning -> informative representations -> better ranking
  - all components trained simultaneously
- Advantages
  - diffusion: inject keyphrase info even during inference
  - ranking network: flexibly extract top k
  - VIB: informative representations, better ranking
  - experiments show importance of each component
- Contributions
  - Diff-KPE; first to use diffusion model for KPE
  - diffusion + ranking network + VIB in one system: use keyphrase + document info
  - outperforms most existing approaches on OpenKP and KP20K; more robust on five small scientific datasets

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Keyphrase extraction (KPE) is about extracting several present keyphrases from a document that can summarize the document well, and this is helpful for many applications such as text summarization and information retrieval.

Many neural keyphrase extraction models treat KPE as a sequence labeling problem at the token level, where they predict a single label for each token. To use the semantic information at the phrase level, some methods model KPE as a phrase classification task and assign labels to each text span.

Recent KPE models are different from these methods: they directly learn to rank each phrase. These methods mainly have two processes, the construction of candidate phrase representations and the ranking of keyphrase importance. The candidate phrase representations are extracted from the token embeddings that pre-trained language models such as BERT produce, and keyphrase importance ranking usually predicts a score for each candidate phrase representation and then uses a margin loss to sort the scores of positive candidates ahead of the negative ones. The candidate phrase representation is important for the model to score them, so there are several ways to extract it: one work uses Bi-LSTM and others use CNN to further capture local-aware features of the phrase. HyperMatch extracts the phrase representation in hyperbolic space.

  - great success on benchmarks, but representations lack reference keyphrase information
  - intuition from humans: review whole document, summarize vague keyphrases in mind, then consider candidate + vague keyphrases
  - challenge: generate vague reference keyphrase info at inference time

  - inject vague keyphrase embeddings into each phrase representation
  - ranking network ranks enhanced representations; extract top k
  - supervised Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB): classification loss per phrase; keep target-class info, filter irrelevant input info (cite); helps learn vague keyphrase embedding

  - all components trained simultaneously

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Keyphrase extraction (KPE) is about extracting several present keyphrases from a document that can summarize the document well, and this is helpful for many applications such as text summarization and information retrieval.

Many neural keyphrase extraction models treat KPE as a sequence labeling problem at the token level, where they predict a single label for each token. To use the semantic information at the phrase level, some methods model KPE as a phrase classification task and assign labels to each text span.

Recent KPE models are different from these methods: they directly learn to rank each phrase. These methods mainly have two processes, the construction of candidate phrase representations and the ranking of keyphrase importance. The candidate phrase representations are extracted from the token embeddings that pre-trained language models such as BERT produce, and keyphrase importance ranking usually predicts a score for each candidate phrase representation and then uses a margin loss to sort the scores of positive candidates ahead of the negative ones. The candidate phrase representation is important for the model to score them, so there are several ways to extract it: one work uses Bi-LSTM and others use CNN to further capture local-aware features of the phrase. HyperMatch extracts the phrase representation in hyperbolic space.

These methods have had great success on many KPE benchmarks, but we point out that their candidate phrase representation still does not use the information of reference keyphrases. The idea comes from how a human extracts candidate phrases: they first review the whole document and summarize a few vague keyphrases in mind, and then they consider both the candidate phrase and the vague keyphrases to decide what to extract. To do this in a neural model, the challenge is how to generate the vague reference keyphrase information at inference time.

To solve this issue we propose Diff-KPE, a novel KPE model based on diffusion. First we use the diffusion model to generate a list of vague keyphrase information, by recovering reference keyphrase embeddings conditioned on the whole document, and then we enhance each phrase representation by injecting the vague keyphrase embeddings into it. To rank the candidate phrases, we apply a ranking network to each enhanced phrase representation. This way we can extract the top k keyphrases we want from the ranked list. We also introduce a supervised Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) to optimize a classification loss for each phrase. Supervised VIB tries to keep the information about the target classes in the latent space and to filter out irrelevant information from the input phrase representation, and this helps to learn the vague keyphrase embedding. Multitask learning with supervised VIB can guide the model to generate informative phrase representations, which improves the performance of the ranking network. Diff-KPE combines these modules by training all the components at the same time.

Because of its architecture design, Diff-KPE has three advantages. First, the diffusion model makes it possible to inject vague keyphrase information into each phrase representation, also during inference, so the model can use keyphrase information. Second, the ranking network ranks each phrase, so we can flexibly extract the top k candidate keyphrases. Finally, the supervised VIB guides the model to generate informative phrase representations, which improves the ranking performance. Our experiments show the importance of each component. The main contributions of this paper are:

- We propose Diff-KPE, a KPE model based on diffusion. As far as we know, this is the first attempt to use the diffusion model for the KPE task.

- We put the diffusion model, ranking network and VIB into one system, so Diff-KPE can use the information of the keyphrases and of the document to extract candidate keyphrases.

- Experiments show that Diff-KPE outperforms most existing KPE approaches on two large keyphrase extraction benchmarks, OpenKP and KP20K. Diff-KPE also shows more robust performance on five other small scientific datasets.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Keyphrase extraction (KPE) aims to extract several present keyphrases from a document that can highly summarize the given document, which is helpful for many applications such as text summarization and information retrieval.

Many neural keyphrase extraction models formulate KPE as a token-level sequence labeling problem by predicting a single label for each token [1,2,3]. To use phrase-level semantic information, some methods [4,5,6,7,8] model KPE as a phrase classification task by assigning labels to each text span.

Different from the above methods, recent KPE models directly learn to rank each phrase [6,9,8,10]. These methods mainly include two processes: candidate phrase representation construction and keyphrase importance ranking. In particular, candidate phrase representations are extracted from the token embeddings produced by pre-trained language models such as BERT [11], and keyphrase importance ranking usually predicts a score for each candidate phrase representation and then uses a margin loss to sort the scores of positive candidates ahead of negative ones. Since the candidate phrase representation is important for the model to score them, there are several ways to extract it: [6] and [8,9] develop Bi-LSTM and CNN, respectively, to further capture local-aware features of the phrase. HyperMatch [10] extracts phrase representations in hyperbolic space.

Although these methods have achieved great success on many KPE benchmarks, we point out that their candidate phrase representation still lacks the use of reference keyphrase information. This is inspired by the intuition of how humans extract candidate phrases: they first review the whole document and summarize a few vague keyphrases in mind, and then take both the candidate phrase and the vague keyphrases into consideration to make the extraction decision. To achieve this process in a neural model, however, the challenge is how to generate the vague reference keyphrase information at inference time.

To address this issue, we propose Diff-KPE, a novel diffusion-based KPE model. We first use the diffusion model to generate a list of vague keyphrase information by recovering reference keyphrase embeddings conditioned on the whole document, and then enhance each phrase representation by injecting the vague keyphrase embeddings into it. To rank candidate phrases, we apply a ranking network to each enhanced phrase representation. In this way, we can extract the desired top k keyphrases from the ranked list of phrases. In addition, we introduce a supervised Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) to optimize a classification loss for each phrase. Supervised VIB aims to preserve the information about the target classes in the latent space while filtering out irrelevant information from the input phrase representation [12], which helps the learning of the vague keyphrase embedding. Multitask learning with supervised VIB can guide the model to generate informative phrase representations, thereby improving the performance of the ranking network. Overall, Diff-KPE combines these modules by training all components simultaneously.

Empowered by its architecture design, Diff-KPE exhibits three advantages. First, the diffusion model enables the injection of vague keyphrase information into each phrase representation, even during inference, giving the model the ability to use keyphrase information. Second, the ranking network ranks each phrase, allowing us to flexibly extract the top k candidate keyphrases. Finally, the supervised VIB guides the model to generate informative phrase representations, improving ranking performance. We demonstrate the importance of each component in our experiments. In summary, the main contributions of this paper are as follows:

- We propose Diff-KPE, a diffusion-based KPE model. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to use the diffusion model for the KPE task.

- By incorporating the diffusion model, ranking network, and VIB into one system, we enable Diff-KPE to use the information of keyphrases and the document to extract candidate keyphrases.

- Experimental results show that Diff-KPE outperforms most existing KPE approaches on two large keyphrase extraction benchmarks, OpenKP and KP20K. Additionally, Diff-KPE shows more robust performance on the other five small scientific datasets.
